bullet_points: Load the observed map, halo catalog, ground-truth CMB map, kSZ map, and noise map.
Compute and print the RMS of each map (observed, CMB truth, kSZ truth, noise, and cleaned residual).
Construct a Wiener filter in Fourier space using the analytical ΛCDM power spectrum formula provided: $D_\ell = 6000 \times (\ell/200)^2 / (1 + (\ell/200)^{1.2})^{2.5} \times \exp(-(\ell/4500)^2)$.
Apply the Wiener filter to the observed map to produce a "cleaned" map.
Save the cleaned map and a diagnostic plot showing the filter transfer function $W(\ell)$ alongside the CMB, noise, and kSZ power spectra.
Extract temperature values at halo pixel positions from both the cleaned map and the raw observed map.
Implement the velocity-weighted cross-correlation estimator $\hat{\tau} = -(c / \langle v_r^2 \rangle) \cdot \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N T_{cleaned, i} \cdot v_{r,i}$.
Incorporate mass-dependent weighting to optimize the signal-to-noise ratio.
Print the recovered mean $\tau$ value and compare it to the catalog mean $\tau$.
Save the per-halo temperature values and the computed pairwise statistics.
Generate a continuous density grid from the halo catalog using a Cloud-in-Cell (CIC) scheme.
Reconstruct line-of-sight peculiar velocities using linear theory (Kaiser formula).
Compare reconstructed velocities against ground-truth $v_{los}$ by computing the Pearson correlation coefficient and RMS residual; print these metrics.
Divide the halo catalog into ten mass bins and calculate the mean optical depth for each bin using the cleaned map temperatures.
Compare recovered $\tau$ per bin to the theoretical $\tau(M) = 2 \times 10^{-3} \times (M/10^{14})^{2/3}$.
Save the reconstructed velocities and binned optical depth results.
Implement a Jackknife resampling procedure over 100 spatial subregions to estimate the covariance matrix of the pairwise kSZ signal.
Perform a null test by shuffling peculiar velocities at least 50 times to produce a distribution of null-test statistics.
Compute and print the detection significance in units of $\sigma$ relative to the null distribution.
Save the covariance matrix and null test results.

Generate a single multi-panel figure including: (a) $\tau-M$ scaling relation with Jackknife error bars and theoretical curve, (b) reconstructed vs. true velocity scatter plot with Pearson $r$, (c) stacked cutout images for low, mid, and high mass bins, and (d) SNR improvement comparison.
Print the fitted slope and normalization of the $\tau-M$ relation with uncertainties.
Save the multi-panel figure to the database path.
Synthesize all quantitative results: fitted $\tau-M$ slope/normalization, velocity reconstruction fidelity (Pearson $r$), detection significance, RMS values, and SNR improvement.
Discuss whether the recovered $\tau-M$ slope is consistent with the input $2/3$ power law.
Interpret the impact of the Wiener filter and the robustness of the statistical detection.
Write the final Results section of the report, summarizing the findings and the performance of the methodology.
